newsitem.title: USA: Calif. withheld nearly $1 bln from fund - court.
newsitem.headline: Calif. withheld nearly $1 bln from fund - court.

text.p: A state appeals court ruled that California improperly withheld nearly $1 billion from the nation's largest public pension fund in order to balance state budgets in the early 1990s.
A spokesperson for California Gov. Pete Wilson said on Friday that the Wilson administration plans to appeal the decision to the state Supreme Court.

In its ruling, the 3rd District Court of Appeal affirmed the 1995 decision of a trial court, which had determined that two laws delaying contributions to the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) were unconstitutional.

In September 1992, the state legislature responded to mounting budget pressure by enacting as urgency legislation Senate Bill 1107, which provided that the state's employer contributions for general fund employees were to be made "semiannually, six months in arrears." In June 1993, Senate Bill 240 was signed into law, providing that employer contributions be made "annually, 12 months in arrears."

As a result of these two measures, employer contributions amounting to $910 million that would have been paid during fiscal years 1992-1993 and 1993-1994 were not paid during those years, the appeals court said in its decision.
In 1994, CalPERS sued the governor and other top state officials, arguing that the measures were unconstitutional.

The trial court hearing the case agreed, ruling in 1995 that "in arrears" financing was an unconstitutional impairment of contract, and directed the governor to disregard Senate Bills 1107 and 240, and to reimburse the retirement fund.
The governor appealed the trial court judgement.

But in its decision, the 3rd District Court of Appeal said CalPERS "members have a contractual right to an actuarially sound retirement system and the 'in arrears' pension financing unconstitutionally impaired that contractual right."
CalPERS welcomed the appeals court decision.

"We are gratified that the court of appeals agreed with the lower court's ruling and our legal interpretation of the issues governing employee pension funds," Pat Macht, a CalPERS spokesperson, said in a statement.
CalPERS is the nation's largest public pension fund, managing assets in excess of $111 billion.
The system provides retirement and health benefits to more than one million active and retired public employees and their families.
